operations.name: Michael Russo

expected.charges: Conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government, under the Smith Act.
expected.sentence:
No conviction — arrested and prosecuted, but the Smith Act case was dismissed in 1957 without a trial verdict.

Verdict as recorded: No — the charges were dismissed in 1957 after the U.S. Supreme Court's Yates v. United States decision; the defendants "won their case."

Charges as recorded: Conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government, under the Smith Act — a McCarthy-era prosecution of Massachusetts Communist Party leaders (the "Bay State Reds") for their political beliefs and association, brought in 1956.

updates.prosecutor: Anthony Julian; George H. Lewald; William S. Kenney; Philip T. White; Lawrence P. McGauley
updates.indicted: May 1956; one count of conspiracy under the Smith Act

operations.source: Primary opinion United States v. Russo, 155 F.Supp.251 (D.Mass.1957): https://case-law.vlex.com/vid/united-states-v-russo-893483575 . Michael A. Russo identified. Motion opinion does not establish final custody disposition; existing dismissal description preserved.

operations.name: Rita Silk Nauni

expected.charges: First-degree murder of a police officer, assault
expected.convicted: First-degree manslaughter and shooting with intent to kill
expected.sentence: One hundred years for manslaughter and fifty years for shooting with intent to kill, affirmed in 1983. This entry records custody before her March 27, 1981 release on appeal bond. The initial admission date remains unresolved. After the bond was revoked she surrendered on April 4 and was again released April 30; that separate interval is recorded in her other case entry. These were interim bail releases, not completion of the sentence.

operations.source: Primary Oklahoma opinion Nauni v. State, 1983 OK CR 136, 670 P.2d126: https://www.oscn.net/applications/oscn/deliverdocument.asp?citeid=6020 . Trial judge identified; appellate counsel not assigned as trial prosecutors. No prison admission inferred from psychiatric hospitalization.
